issue.title: Implement Offline Chapter Claiming on First Recording
issue.body:
When a translator is offline, claiming works the same way as online — the first recording on an unassigned chapter implicitly claims it — but the claim is held in local device state and cannot be confirmed with the server until reconnect. This ticket implements the offline claiming path: detect the first recording on an unassigned chapter while offline, update local state, and reflect the provisional claim in the chapter row. Reconnect sync and conflict detection are handled in a follow-on ticket.

## Functional Requirements

### Auto-Claim on First Recording (Offline)

- When a translator creates the first recording on an unassigned chapter while offline, mark the chapter as claimed in local device state with no confirmation prompt.
- Update the chapter row to the "mine" state (`li:user`, primary color `#0b50d0`); the claim is provisional until synced.
- Derive the chapter's available/taken/assigned state from last-synced data; do not make a live server check.

Note: The "mine" state visual treatment is defined and mocked up in #267. An unassigned chapter (per last-synced state) may be recorded on by a second offline translator simultaneously — the device has no way to detect or prevent this until reconnect. Conflict detection on reconnect is handled in #271.

comments.body:
### Eng note (updated)

Provisional local “mine” while offline is still this ticket’s core (last-synced unassigned → local claim). Confirm/sync is **#271** + **eten-tech-foundation/fluent-api#272**.

**Preferred:** shape the local queue so it plugs into `fluent-api#272` and try to land offline claim + API claim as one feature with #268/#271.

**Fallback:** ship local-only provisional claim with mocked confirm if API is too heavy — don’t half-implement a claim endpoint from this ticket.
